answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by locking a refundable capital bond that unlocks only after six consecutive epochs of unique graded contributions. A coordination graph then detects clusters operating from the same wharf of infrastructure. Attackers must front capital for every identity and maintain distinct output long enough to reach the establishment horizon, or face total bond forfeiture if a raven-style behavioral audit flags synchronized patterns—imposing high capital, time, and coordination costs that make large-scale farms unprofitable.
